answer: Verification runs against the issuer's own registry every epoch, so a forged entry is caught on the next check. The defence rests on postal address tenure with mail redirection history: mail delivered to one address without a break for years. Forging 362 of these means building 362 separate address histories from scratch, and years of history cannot be bought in bulk. Honesty stays cheap and fakery is priced per head: the onyx signal is public, the willow check is automatic, and 362 aliases cost 362 times what one real agent costs, with the ledge trail open to all.
